title: With Keyboard Remapping, source keys are also triggered
author: chikai-ito

status.label: Need current load-specific repro
status.detail: The report says key remaps sometimes also emit the source key, and the author suspects high memory load. It is from PowerToys 0.76.2 and has no current-build test.

next_action: Request a current-build repro with the mapping, target app, and load conditions before proposing an input-hook change.

judgment.rationale: The issue describes source and target keys both appearing intermittently and the author later suspects heavy application memory use, but provides no controlled reproduction, current version, or diagnostic capture. Related #32954 concerns browser-specific numpad output but does not confirm the same source-key leak or a covering fix.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.76.2 and gives 3 to 4 as an example where source key 3 sometimes also appears in a text editor.
The author later said the problem seemed associated with heavy memory use and could be resolved by closing resource-heavy tasks such as Chrome.
Related open issue #32954 describes numpad remaps producing wrong digits in browsers but does not establish a common cause or fix.
There is no current-build retest, exact load measurement, or attached diagnostic report in the thread.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a current-build retest of a single source-to-target mapping under normal and high-load conditions, with exact target app and a fresh /bugreport if the source leaks again.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported build is 0.76.2 and the load correlation is unverified. No code change should be proposed until a current reproduction confirms the source-key leak and its conditions.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager sometimes emits both the source key and its remapped target; the author suspects the issue occurs under heavy memory use.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.76.2 and says source key 3 sometimes appears along with its target 4 in a text editor.
The author later said closing resource-heavy applications such as Chrome could resolve the problem.
The issue has two comments and no assignee or current-build reproduction.
inferences: High system load could affect low-level input processing, but the report does not establish a hook timeout, dropped event, or other specific cause.
The browser-specific numpad symptom in #32954 may be related at a broad input-remapping level but is not a confirmed duplicate.
issue_context.analysis: The source-key leak is distinct from a remap that simply stops working, and the author's load observation is useful but unmeasured. Ask for the same mapping under normal and high load on a current build, then collect diagnostics immediately after a failure rather than attributing it to memory pressure.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and both comments, including the author's suspected high-memory correlation.
Checked open related issue #32954; its browser-specific numpad symptom does not establish the same failure or a covering fix.
No linked fix or direct duplicate was established.

information_gaps.information: Whether source-key leakage persists on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer, with the exact source-to-target mapping, target app, and a comparison under normal versus high load.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is intermittent and the proposed memory-load correlation has not been isolated from the target application or mapping.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest one simple mapping in Notepad on 0.100.2 or newer under normal conditions and while the suspected heavy application is running; note whether source and target both appear.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after a current source-key leak.
information_gaps.why_needed: Current Keyboard Manager configuration and engine diagnostics may distinguish dropped suppression from a target-app issue.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If source and target both appear, comment /bugreport immediately after reproducing.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. It describes source key 3 appearing alongside its remapped target 4 and notes that closing resource-heavy apps may help. To determine whether this is still reproducible, could you please provide:
1. A retest on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer, naming the exact source-to-target mapping and target app.
2. Whether the source key leaks under normal conditions and when the suspected heavy application is running.
3. If it still occurs, a fresh diagnostic archive by commenting `/bugreport` immediately after the failure.
This will separate a current input-hook issue from app-specific or load-related behavior.
